prompt:
You are a Kilo native Pi agent invoked as an independent peer on a separate provider platform. Perform a read-only, architecture-level review of OmniRoute-evan. The workflow supplies a baseline snapshot of release/v3.8.54 and a candidate snapshot of agent-router-a2a-20261112-06. Do not run tests or modify files.

DESIGN TARGET
A durable, self-replenishing heterogeneous agent federation with genuine provider-native agent turns and agent-to-agent handoffs. Preserve the existing ownership boundaries:
- Pipeline: the single recurring-work scheduler, leases, retries, effect readback.
- WorkEpisode: durable task/turn record, parent-child lineage and evidence.
- Networks & Federation: provider selection, placement, resource inventory and independent capacity.
- Accounts & Secrets: encrypted credential custody and least-privilege identity.
- ComputerUseX: browser sessions, provider UI automation and sanitized HAR evidence.
- B4PT0R: provider-native execution and native task/session lifecycle.
- LibreChat Agents: API-native agent graphs.
- OmniRoute: model routing/inference and MCP/A2A gateway.

OBSERVED EXECUTION EVIDENCE
1. Agent Router run 43270370904 completed. TaskPlanner native task 48da48ab-3d98-4b1f-a651-2d3b652bd03b returned provider state COMPLETED. SoftwareEngineeringExpert and the selected 36% ResearchAgent call returned HTTP 502; do not count either as completed.
2. The same run made a separate A2A call to https://social.duoleads.com/a2a. It returned STATE completed and context ID 1ea9310c-222f-40f4-a662-c544e482e9cf, but only supplied public capability/pricing information. No paid data skill or USDC payment was invoked.
3. Historical branch agent-router-a2a-20261112-04 has verified completed native tasks: constructivecritic task c9f60e8b-5428-45d5-a791-76cda7887ea2 and firstprinciplesanalyst task 3d4c77ec-0df2-460f-9874-2e735b1a7317. Its sanitized HAR and receipt were retained in workflow run 43243289067.
4. Branches -05 and -06 added same-task resumption and richer receipts. In run 43256816127, a TaskPlanner result with structured state COMPLETED was misclassified as pending because its natural-language response also contained the word PENDING. Its secondary agent was therefore suppressed. Branch -06 also recorded a completed free preflight A2A call to https://shop.lordevo.com/a2a, but the target site was robots-disallowed.
5. The current release workflow uses Math.random() for its 36% secondary-agent branch and has broad free-text pending detection. A retry must preserve the same selection and must not create duplicate native tasks.
6. Browser evidence from run 43270370904: Agent Router pricing HTTP 200 and says $0/no signup for normal use; MCP endpoint https://www.agent-router.org/mcp-http/mcp returned HTTP 200; 27 tools discovered. DeepWiki pages returned HTTP 429 and were not read.
7. Existing Vercel Hobby infrastructure has a large stopped sandbox fleet and seven persistent snapshots. Attempting to resume networks-browser-acquisition-b returned resource_creation_blocked (HTTP 402). Do not evade this provider restriction by creating duplicate accounts or switching identities. GitHub Actions is an available independent remote runner.

REVIEW QUESTIONS
A. Compare current release/v3.8.54 against historical candidate -06. Which proven implementation should be promoted, and which parts should be composed rather than wholesale-reverted? Use exact file paths and function names.
B. Define a typed provider-terminal-state contract. Structured provider state must outrank natural-language response content; distinguish task status from result text. Specify precedence for COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT, RUNNING, QUEUED, and UNKNOWN, including provider readback and explicit error envelopes.
C. Design deterministic 36% secondary-agent selection that is stable across retries and workflow replays, with exactly one idempotency key per WorkEpisode and no duplicate child task. Explain how to measure the cadence over time without using Math.random().
D. Specify the minimum durable native-turn receipt: provider/platform, agent, native task/session ID, parent WorkEpisode, invocation idempotency key, request/response digests, timestamps, terminal state, readback evidence, and effect status.
E. Recommend the highest-value integration seam across Pipeline, WorkEpisode, Networks, Accounts, ComputerUseX and B4PT0R. Do not introduce another scheduler or replace the current owners.
F. Evaluate Kilo as an additional provider-native execution platform and how its free model route should integrate as a B4PT0R/Networks worker without owning scheduling. If your runtime has a real native A2A tool to a different platform, you may perform one free/read-only task and independently read back its terminal state; otherwise explicitly report that this capability is unavailable. Do not simulate a handoff.
G. Identify a robust fallback strategy for HTTP 502, unavailable providers, 429/rate limits and Vercel resource_creation_blocked that preserves quotas, task identity and provider ownership. No account-creation or quota-evasion recommendations.
H. Review the existing revenue-bounty-scout workflow as a separate lane: identify the path from a genuinely new posted bounty/contract to completed work and settlement, without outreach, selling offerings, or treating existing earnings as new revenue.

OUTPUT
Return observed facts separately from recommendations and unknowns. Prioritize one long-term integration seam, list exact repository paths, provide a concise dependency/ownership diagram in text, and state whether you actually triggered any successor agent. Cite the supplied workflow IDs and native IDs. No code changes, commits, tests, paid actions, account creation, secret access, or credential output.
